summary: npm package ships a browser-side fake-Cloudflare redirect page as its only content
details: The package contains a single file, index.html, declared as `main`. The page renders a spoofed Cloudflare 'Just a moment...' / Turnstile 'security verification' interstitial (fake Ray ID alongside a real Turnstile widget) and, on completion, runs an obfuscator.io-wrapped script that assembles a URL starting with 'https://lo' + decoded fragments + '/', appends the current query string, and navigates window.location to it. No install lifecycle scripts (preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare) are declared and `main` points at a non-JS file, so `npm install` and `require()` do not execute any code on a developer machine or build system. The hostile behavior only manifests if a browser is pointed at index.html. This is registry abuse for hosting phishing/redirect infrastructure rather than a supply-chain attack against installers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
